skill_reference: skill is the Brier skill against the P0 base rate of the FULL history at the final origin (the reference of the main table), the same for every point; skill_own_base is against the base rate of each point's own subsample
paired_vs_p1_note: per fraction, the mean over seeds of the paired difference from P1 on the same held-out rows: logscore_minus_p1 is the rung's log score minus P1's (nats per row, above zero is better), brier_gain_over_p1 is P1's Brier score minus the rung's (above zero is better); the interval is the percentile interval of the seed-averaged by-test resamples, as for the skill
paired_vs_full_note: per fraction below 1, the mean over seeds of the paired difference of a rung fitted on the subsample from the same rung fitted on the full history, on the same held-out rows: logscore_minus_full is the subsample's log score minus the full history's (nats per row, below zero means the smaller history is worse), brier_gain_over_full is the full history's Brier score minus the subsample's (below zero means the smaller history is worse); the interval is the percentile interval of the seed-averaged by-test resamples, with the resamples of paired_vs_p1 (design: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-10-history-amount-comparison.md)
command: moot backtest --source upworthy --origins quarterly --challenger gbm --challenger local_eb --challenger text_lr --seed 0 --learning-curve 0.01,0.02,0.05,0.1,0.25,0.5,1 --seeds 20
